fields.meta_title: Influencer Landing Page Builder for Campaigns | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an influencer landing page from a prompt: a waitlist page per creator, an ambassador form, product gifting, and a campaign brief.
fields.h1: Build an Influencer Landing Page for Every Creator You Work With
fields.hero_description: Build an influencer landing page for each creator in a campaign, and save every signup under that creator's name.
fields.features_heading: What a Creator Program Needs From Its Pages
fields.features_subheading: An influencer landing page is where a creator's followers land after the post. Emergent builds that page and the records behind it.
fields.feature_1:
One page per creator, from one prompt

Describe the campaign once and Emergent builds a page for each creator: their photo, a line in their own words, and their code. Add a fourth creator later with another prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Every signup filed under its creator

The app saves each signup to a database you own, with the creator's name and the time it came in. Sort by creator at the end of the week to see whose followers came through.
fields.feature_3:
Applicant rules written in plain words

Put the rule in the prompt, such as a follower count or a niche, and the app sends an email or Slack alert to whoever handles that applicant, with the answers in the message.
fields.feature_4:
Signups passed to the tools you run

The app connects to any tool with an API. Signups can go to your email platform and gifting picks to the tool that ships them, and the data syncs in and out both ways.
fields.feature_5:
Creator pages at the brand's address

Publish each creator's page as a path on the brand's domain, and the address a creator reads out or pins belongs to the brand. Custom domains are included and use credits.
fields.feature_6:
The code in your GitHub, on paid plans

Export every page's code to your GitHub repository on paid plans and keep building on it in your own stack. Free to start: the free tier covers building and publishing.

fields.tab_content_1:
For the serum waitlist, Noor's page drew 540 signups

Saltbirch Skin is launching a barrier serum with three creators, each linking to a waitlist page with their photo and their code. Every signup is saved with the creator's name. Of 1,180 signups in the first week, Noor Adeyemi's page drew 540, Tessa Lindqvist's 410, and Caleb Brandt's 230.
fields.tab_content_2:
At 10,000 followers or more, an application goes to Ines

Creators apply to Fieldline Outdoor's ambassador program on one page: handle, main platform, follower count, and niche. An applicant with 10,000 followers or more is emailed to Ines Moravec, who runs partnerships. Smaller accounts stay in the applicants table for her monthly review.
fields.tab_content_3:
Within a week, 60 of 75 creators had picked a roast

Brightwick Coffee sends its new roasts to 75 creators it has already approved, through a private gifting page. Each creator picks a roast and a grind and enters a shipping address. Every pick becomes a row in the shipping table that Orla Fenn packs from. Within a week, 60 of the 75 had made a pick.
fields.tab_content_4:
Jonah is the one creator still to confirm the brief

Wavecrest Swim's brief page gives each of its 8 creators one Reel and two Stories, then asks them to confirm the posts will disclose the partnership. The FTC's guide for social media influencers says to place the disclosure with the endorsement message itself. So far, 7 of 8 have confirmed; Jonah Pryce gets a reminder.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Influencer Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Follow seven steps to plan an influencer landing page for each creator, build it from a prompt, and test it before the first post.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the one action the page asks for
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write the creator into the page
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Describe every page in one prompt
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose one job for the page: a waitlist signup, an application, a gifting pick, or a brief to confirm. A follower who taps through has seen one post from one creator. Give the page one headline and one button that match that post.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask each creator for a photo and one line about the product in their own words, and put their code near the top. A visitor who arrives from Noor's post should see Noor on the page, not a stock product shot.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Tell Emergent who the creators are and what happens after a submit: which table keeps the entry and who gets an alert. Emergent builds every creator page and the table behind them from that one prompt, and a later prompt changes the fields.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Give each creator a link with utm_source, utm_medium, and utm_campaign, plus utm_content set to the creator's name. Google Analytics says to always use those first three whenever you add parameters to a URL.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Decide who hears about each entry
fields.howto_step_5_des: Name one person for each kind of entry. Applicants over your follower count go to the partnerships lead, and gifting picks go to whoever packs orders. Entries that need nobody today still land in the table for later review.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test it from a creator's link
fields.howto_step_6_des: Open each creator's page on a phone from the tagged link, submit a test signup, and check that the row carries the right creator name and campaign value. Delete the test rows before the first post goes live.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Compare creators after the first week
fields.howto_step_7_des: Sort the week's entries by creator and by campaign value, and set each creator's signups against what the partnership cost. Keep the creators whose pages convert, and send the next campaign brief to them first.

faq_plan.q: What is an influencer landing page?
faq_plan.a: An influencer landing page is the page a creator's followers reach when they tap the link in a sponsored post. It carries that creator's face and code, asks for one action, such as a waitlist signup, and records which creator sent each visitor.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an influencer landing page?
faq_plan.a: Describe the creators and the one action each page asks for in a prompt to Emergent's AI landing page builder. It builds a page per creator and the database behind them. Then tag each creator's link, test a signup from a phone, and publish.

faq_plan.q: What should a creator landing page include for a brand campaign?
faq_plan.a: A creator landing page for a campaign needs five things: a headline that matches the post, the creator's photo, a sentence from the creator on why they use it, their code, and one form. Leave out the full catalog. A visitor from one post came for one product.

faq_plan.q: Can I build an influencer landing page for my own audience?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent builds your own page from a prompt, such as a fan email list or a brand inquiry form, with every entry in a database you own. A musician promoting shows and releases is better served by an artist landing page.

faq_plan.q: Should each creator in a campaign get their own influencer landing page?
faq_plan.a: Yes, whenever the campaign has more than one creator. A page per creator shows that creator's face and code, and every signup arrives tagged with their name, which makes the end-of-campaign comparison a sort rather than a guess. One shared page works only when every link carries a creator tag.

faq_plan.q: How do I track which creator sent a signup on an influencer landing page?
faq_plan.a: Use two signals: the page or tagged link the visitor arrived on, and the code they enter at checkout. The app saves the creator's name with each signup, and a creator's code entered at checkout ties a later purchase to that creator as well.

faq_plan.q: Can an influencer landing page sell a creator's online course?
faq_plan.a: It can take signups for one, but selling a course needs more than a campaign page: a syllabus and an enrollment form with the price. Build that as a course landing page, point the creator's posts to it, and carry the creator's code through to enrollment.

faq_plan.q: How do I recruit creators with an influencer landing page?
faq_plan.a: Put an application page on the brand's site and link it from the brand's own profiles. Ask for links to two recent posts as well as the follower count: the posts show whether a creator's audience fits the product. Emergent can build the reply too, an email that tells each applicant what happens next.

faq_plan.q: Can an influencer landing page handle free product requests?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent can build a private gifting page where each approved creator picks a product and enters a shipping address. The app saves each pick as a row to ship from. Mention disclosure in the invite: the FTC's Disclosures 101 guide counts a brand giving free or discounted products as a relationship to disclose.

faq_plan.q: Do influencer landing pages work for podcast sponsorships?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Give the host a short page address to read out, and put the host's code on the page. Listeners type the address rather than tap it, which means it has to be short and easy to spell. If the show needs a home of its own, that is a podcast landing page.

plan.angle: The top 10 for influencer landing page is design galleries (Behance, Dribbble, Figma, Webflow showcases) plus three builder guides; the guides describe the page as a bridge from a creator's post to a brand's offer, and two cover recruiting creators, but none shows what happens to the visitor after the tap. This page is written for the brand running a creator program and shows four influencer landing pages built from a prompt: one page per creator that saves each signup under that creator's name, an application page that routes larger creators to the partnerships lead, a private gifting page that turns product picks into shipping rows, and a campaign brief page where each creator confirms the deliverables and the disclosure. It stays clear of the link-in-bio, personal and artist pages, which cover a creator's own page.
